findings.title: `self.downsize` is redefined, overwriting the 4/5-argument version
findings.body: Ruby does not support method overloading by arity. Defining `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` on line 149 completely overwrites `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` on line 145. Any existing caller passing `(from, to, max_width, max_height)` (or 5 arguments with `opts`) will now either pass `max_height` as `opts` (causing `TypeError: no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer` when `opts[:allow_animation]` is evaluated on a numeric `max_height`) or fail with `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (given 5, expected 3..4)`.

findings.title: Client-side size check ignores `max_attachment_size_kb` for non-image uploads
findings.body: `validateUploadedFile` previously checked `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, which enforced `max_attachment_size_kb` for non-image attachments and `max_image_size_kb` for images. Replacing this with a hard-coded `10 * 1024` (10 MB) for all upload types means non-image attachments are no longer validated against `max_attachment_size_kb` on the client (even though the server will not downsize attachments and will still reject them or conversely allow larger attachments than configured until the upload completes).

findings.title: `tempfile.size` is cached on open Ruby `Tempfile`/`File` objects or not refreshed after external modification
findings.body: In `create_upload`, `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` modifies the file on disk via an external `convert`/`gifsicle` process while `tempfile` is an open `Tempfile` handle. Additionally, if `OptimizedImage.downsize` fails (for example, on an SVG, WebP without delegate, corrupt image, or animated GIF when `--resize-fit 80%` is rejected by `gifsicle`), `downsize` returns `false` without shrinking the file, yet the loop still runs all 5 attempts unconditionally instead of breaking on failure.

findings.title: `gifsicle --resize-fit` does not accept percentage dimensions like `"80%"`
findings.body: `UploadsController` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`. When an animated GIF is uploaded and `allow_animation` is enabled, `downsize_instructions_animated` delegates to `resize_instructions_animated`, which runs `gifsicle ... --resize-fit 80%`. `gifsicle`'s `--resize-fit` option requires `WxH` pixel dimensions (unlike `--scale`), so passing `"80%"` causes `gifsicle` to exit with an error on every attempt and leaves the GIF unresized.
